Play the free Matchy Star demo now, ahead of Steam Next Fest (October 19–26, 2026). Wishlist Matchy Star to follow its journey!

Matchy Star is a colorful match-3 roguelite where your ship’s flight path shapes every move. Match stars, collect quirky upgrades, and chart a changing route through space toward Xanadu.

Instead of matching anywhere you want, every move is shaped by your ship’s flight path. Plan ahead, collect the right stars, chain together big matches, and keep your bubbly little ships moving through a giant galaxy of puzzle challenges.

Travel from Star Base all the way to the legendary Xanadu, meeting a cast of goofy cosmic friends, derpy stars, stylish ships, and powerful items along the way.

Match Stars. Power Ships. Reach Xanadu.

Your ships,  Zippy, Skippy, and Bob, each follow their own path through space. To move forward, you need to match stars along the route, extend your range, and collect enough power to survive the journey.

The better your matches, the stronger your run becomes. Big chains, smart planning, and the right item combinations can turn a humble little ship into the fanciest hero in the galaxy.

Build Your Perfect Space Swag

Collect items with stat boosts to customize your ships and improve your chances. Grab crowns, monocles, beards, swords, and other ridiculous cosmic gear. Your ships are fancy. They are special. They deserve proper swag.

Items can affect your score, speed, fuel, buffer alerts, and other important stats, giving each run its own personality and strategy.

Meet the Matchyverse Crew

Zippy is the biggest and slowest ship, but he makes up for it by baking the best cookies in space. Skippy is mid-sized, speedy, and holds the record for eating the most cookies in under a minute. Bob is the smallest and fastest, and for reasons nobody understands, he likes burnt cookies.

Along the way, they are joined by familiar faces from the Matchyverse, including Matchy Star, Spacey Galaxy, Speedy Sputnik, Doctor UFO, Guru Moon, and Pirate Planet.

A Cute Puzzle Game With Real Strategy

Matchy Star is cheerful, silly, and easy to enjoy, but later levels will test your planning. Power-ups, ship stats, items, and star collection all matter as the journey gets tougher.

Features include:

  • Classic match-3 inspiration with a path-based twist

  • Try to complete a run through a randomly generated path of different planets, and procedurally generated and pre-designed levels, buffs, and debuffs.

  • Collect all the items; each one has a unique effect on how the game plays, like bonuses to movement or matches of different shapes.

  • Three playable ships: Zippy, Skippy, and Bob

  • Big chains, score bonuses, power-ups, and strategic item choices

  • A bright, silly, cozy world full of cosmic nonsense

Welcome Back to the Matchyverse

If you enjoyed MatchyGotchy or Matchy’s Kooky Cookies, Matchy Star brings that cute, colorful world back in a bigger puzzle adventure.

Help Matchy Star reach Xanadu, because last time he was there, he forgot his wallet.

It is time to get your Matchy on.

Thank you for playing. You are what keeps the Matchyverse alive ~☆

Math Defense Protocol is a strategy game that combines mathematical formula building, character team composition, and tower defense combat.

Build Powerful Turrets with Numbers and Operators

On the battlefield, numbers are more than just resources. Drag numbers and mathematical operators into your turrets' formula slots to create combinations using addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and more.

Your Calculations Determine Your Firepower

The results of your calculations directly affect your turrets' levels, attack power, and combat performance. Will you prioritize consistent damage or take risks to unleash devastating firepower? Every formula and every strategic decision is yours to make.

Recruit Characters and Create Powerful Team Synergies

Recruit and deploy a diverse cast of characters, each with unique roles, abilities, and synergies. Carefully position your units and build effective team compositions to defend against ever-changing enemy waves and challenging stage mechanics.

Uncover Lost Memories in a Fractured World of Consciousness

The story takes place in a world of consciousness slowly being consumed by corruption. Journey through fragmented memories, unlock character backstories, and uncover the truth behind Christine and her companions as you fight your way through the story.

Story Campaign, Endless Tower Climbing, and More Challenges

The adventure doesn't end with the main story. Take on endless tower-climbing challenges and additional game modes to push your mathematical strategies and team compositions to their limits.

A game made by a dad, with ideas from his 4- and 5-year-old kids.

Rescue and collect plastic ducks with crazy superpowers, then use them to wreak havoc!

Mayhem Duck Simulator is a physics-based rubber duck simulator that turns a quiet poolside into total chaos. Set the pool on fire with the dragon duck, get the whole pool dancing with the disco duck, or sit back and watch the ducks cause trouble on their own. Float calmly on the water or smash everything in your path: the choice is yours!

FREE THEM, USE THEIR POWERS

Every special duck has a power of its own. Switch to a duck you've freed from its cage and unleash it: lift ducks into the sky with a UFO beam, grow a tail of ducks behind you with the magnet, or turn ducks into giants with the wizard. Dragon, fireworks, helicopter, disco and more are waiting for you.

FIND THE KEY, OPEN THE CAGE

Special ducks are locked away in cages. Walk up to them and they'll turn to you and ask for help. Find the key, bring it to the cage and set the duck free. Every duck you rescue joins your collection, and you can switch to it and play whenever you like.

CAUSE MAYHEM

Dash through windows and shatter the glass, grab objects with your beak and throw them, knock down palm trees. Charge up and launch yourself, and every duck and object in your way goes flying. Everything runs on physics, so even a small bump can set off a chain reaction of chaos.

COLLECT, PAINT AND NAME YOUR DUCKS

New ducks keep arriving and joining your collection as you play. Try to collect them all, then grab a brush and paint your ducks however you like. Give each one a name and see it appear above its head in the game.

OR JUST WATCH

Leave the game alone for a while and it switches to Watch Mode. The ducks swim around, use their powers and talk to each other in emojis. Sit back and watch day turn into night, or leave the game running on your second monitor like an aquarium.

This game is for you if:

  • You want a fun plastic duck simulator to unwind with, without complicated mechanics

  • You want to unleash your inner chaos in the middle of a relaxing game

  • You love physics-based comedy, absurd moments and sandbox fun

In Mayhem Duck Simulator, you'll either find your inner peace or create glorious chaos. Your choice!

A NOTE FROM THE DEVELOPER

Welcome to the imagination of my 4- and 5-year-old kids!

I developed Mayhem Duck Simulator on my own. My day job is 3D environment art, and I learned Blueprints in Unreal Engine 5 just to be able to finish this game.

It all started when I bought my kids that famous plastic duck game. They love playing with rubber ducks in the bath, and they loved the game too. But ten times a day, they asked me the same question: "Dad, why can't we move the ducks?" Anyone with a 5-year-old knows that question never stops.

So I made one duck move and let them play. They loved it, and of course it didn't stop there: "Dad, make a UFO duck!", "Make a firework duck!", "Make a popcorn duck!", "Make a disco duck!" In the end, they're the ones who made me finish this game.

I never interfered with their ideas. Whatever they asked for, I made. They were also my toughest testers. This game is a keepsake for them too: when they grow up, they'll see that every duck they dreamed up really became a game. I hope you enjoy their imagination as much as I do.

FREE UPDATES AND YOUR IDEAS

I'm always open to constructive feedback and new duck ideas. Share yours in the Steam Community Hub, and I'll go through every one of them together with my kids. Who knows, maybe the next special duck will be your idea! I'll keep updating the game, and all updates will be completely free. I will never sell any of them as DLC.

If you enjoy the game, leaving a short review on Steam means a lot to a solo developer. Your support helps this little duck world keep growing.

Mechanis Obscura is a first-person psychological escape-room thriller game, that fuses the intensity of real escape rooms with the atmosphere of early 2000s horror films. Featuring FMV cutscenes filmed in the heart of the city of  Thessaloniki, intricate puzzle mechanisms, and ARG elements that bleed beyond the screen, the game challenges players to survive a trial they never meant to join.

The Plot

It begins in August 2025. Late at night, while browsing forgotten online forums, you unknowingly enroll in something you should never have touched. Days later, you are abducted by a secret underground organization and forced into a mechanical labyrinth hidden beneath the city. Every door locked, every mechanism ticking, every scene whispering that you were chosen for reasons still obscured.

No Choices

This is not a story of choice. There are no branching paths or alternate fates. Mechanis Obscura is built on one relentless truth: escape or vanish.  Along the way, you’ll uncover fragments of the organization’s presence sometimes hidden deep underground, sometimes standing in plain sight.

The Game in the Game

With its blend of puzzles, live-action sequences, and a suffocating atmosphere, Mechanis Obscura blurs the line between game and reality. What begins as an abduction soon becomes a descent into something larger, where the most obscure machinery might be the human mind itself.

Key Features

  • Psychological Horror – A thriller inspired by early 2000s underground horror and their unsettling mood.

  • Escape-Room Adventure – Navigate gears, locks, and lethal contraptions.

  • Mind-Bending Puzzles – Intricate mechanisms and escape-room-style riddles that twist perception as much as intellect.

  • Live-Action Storytelling – FMV and live-action sequences woven into gameplay for a chilling, cinematic feel.

  • Deep Web & Abduction Themes – Uncover how you were taken—and why.

  • ARG Elements – Extend the experience beyond the game into hidden trails and real-world puzzles.

  • Atmospheric Exploration – Every corridor hides secrets, every choice leaves a mark.

  • Rooted in Reality – A narrative set in Thessaloniki, beginning August 2025.

In Medieval Ascendant, you write your own saga in the harsh medieval world of the fantasy realm Aldred. You begin as a simple serf with no possessions and fight your way up through the rigid social hierarchy over generations. When your character passes away, your legacy lives on in your heir. Each generation decides the rise or fall of your dynasty.

Tend your fields, master a craft, or dominate the market and build a vast production network across five unique provinces. Shape the realm to your liking through supremacy in economy, war, or intrigue. Whether you ultimately ascend the throne through bloody campaigns, dark scheming, or the ruthless power of coin is entirely up to you. rn

Key Features:

  • Your rise from a rightless serf to the heights of nobility across multiple generations

  • A fantasy realm with five individual provinces and simulated population

  • Fully simulated economy influenced by weather, plagues, and war

  • Conquer land by the sword, through cunning intrigue, or economic ruin

  • Strategic warfare and tactical battles that leave lasting wounds

  • Unique stories and unpredictable dialogues in every playthrough

Found your dynasty and climb the feudal social order over generations. Full patriarchal system with genetics, inheritance, education, and strategic alliances through marriage and dowry.

Five provinces with local markets, population-driven demand, prosperity, NPC competitors who influence the market, and seasonal fluctuations. Droughts, plagues, and wars affect the economy. Use your economic power to make provinces flourish or starve.

Multiple production chains to manufacture every available good in the game. Each province offers unique advantages for producing certain goods. Build houses for the population, but make sure there are enough homeless to occupy your houses.

Wage war against rival houses or defend the realm against invading neighbors. Every battle carries the risk that your character dies or is permanently injured. Each battle spans multiple rounds — watch your breathing, for an exhausted character is easily wounded. Prepare yourself and equip your character with weapon, armor, and shield.

Death is not the end. Your legacy is carried on through the generations. Customize your playstyle by focusing on economy, combat, diplomacy, intrigue, or dynasty. Multi-tiered development of legacies.

Megachest is an incremental game about opening chests, discovering legendary loot, and building your ultimate fortune empire!

                 

               

Features

  • Satisfying clicker and idle progression

  • Loot legendary loot and manage biggest inventory ever

  • Hire helper to automate chests opening

  • Discover new chests and unique loot

  • Prestige to earn powerful permanent relics

  • Watch your inventory grow while you're away

MEGASHOOTSPLOSION

A fast, physics-drunk arena shooter where the fight keeps changing under your feet. Start simple. Do not stay simple.

You spawn with a clean loadout and a fair fight. Then the upgrades start stacking. Bouncing projectiles, absurd knockback, extra air time, momentum that flings you across the map, and a tidy little duel turns into beautiful chaos. Every match writes its own rules as it goes.

THROW YOUR GUN TO RELOAD

There's no reload button. When you're empty, you chuck the gun at the other guy. It hurts if it lands, and a fresh one drops into your hands a second later. Some upgrades even trigger off the throw itself, so your empty mag becomes a weapon and a plan.

MOVE LIKE YOU MEAN IT

Sprint, slide, and wall-jump all flow into each other. Slide-jump to keep your speed, kick off a wall to change the angle, and stay a moving target. In this game, footwork is half the gunfight.

LOSE A ROUND, GET STRONGER

In Upgrade Battle, the loser picks an upgrade that sticks for the rest of the match. Falling behind doesn't bury you. It hands you the tools to swing back. Upgrades combine in ways nobody planned, and no two builds feel the same.

RUN THE GAUNTLET

Eight solo fights, one on every map, each with its own mode and twist: a warm-up duel, a Gun Game race, a 2v2 with a bot on your side, a low-gravity brawl where throwing is the only attack, and a final stage where every hit kills. Fewer deaths earn more stars, and stars unlock body colours you can't get anywhere else.

FLIP ON SOME CHAOS

Stack match mutators on any mode, online or against bots:

  •  Big Heads: Giant heads, easier headshots. It never stops being funny.

  •  One Shot: Every hit kills.

  • Throws Only: Guns spawn empty. The throw is your only attack.

  • Low Gravity: Floaty jumps, long falls, rocket jumps into orbit.

PICK YOUR POISON. 8 MODES.

1v1 Duels

  •  Upgrade Battle: Loser picks an upgrade each set. First to 3 sets takes it.

  •  Loadout Battle: Build your starting kit, then throw down.

  • Chaos Randomizer: Random items every set. Adapt or die.

  • Gun Game: Score a kill with every weapon tier to win.

  • Quick Duel: No gimmicks. Pure aim, first to the target.

Up to 4 Players

  •  FFA Deathmatch: Everyone for themselves. First to the kill target.

  • Team Deathmatch: 2v2, first team to the number.

  • Last Man Standing: No respawns. Be the one left standing.

NOBODY ONLINE? BRING BOTS.

Every mode plays offline against AI fighters on three difficulties, from a 1v1 duel to a 2v2 with a bot partner. Hosting online with a seat still empty? Fill it with bots and start anyway. Or warm up in the Practice Range.

LEVEL UP AND SHOW IT OFF

Online matches earn XP toward a 100-level track of titles, body colours and, at the very top, a custom colour mixer. Three daily challenges pay bonus XP. Pick the game up before December 1 for the exclusive Founder colour.

Quick to pick up. Ridiculous once it gets going. Grab a friend and find out how weird one match can get.

Koharu is a girl with no power to fight. In pursuit of her father's shadow, she borrows the strength of monsters and sets out for the summit of a colossal tower.

Memento Resonance is a monster-collecting roguelite turn-based strategy game centered on forging Resonance with monsters, customizing skills with relics, responding to telegraphed enemy actions, and following the trail of lost memories.

Welcome Enemies as Allies Through Resonance


The monsters that inhabit the tower are more than foes to defeat.

Offer them food in battle to lower their guard, and if Resonance succeeds, they can join you as new allies.

At the end of each adventure, choose one of the monsters that joined you through Resonance to bring back to your base and take with you on your next journey. Each monster has a signature skill unique to its species, as well as passive skills that vary from one individual to another.

Even monsters of the same species have their own quirks. Find a favorite and climb toward the summit together.

Customize Skills with Relics


Relics found in the tower can be socketed into your monsters' skills.

Boost their power, add Shield, or combine status effects with special conditions—the same skill can play a different role depending on the relics equipped. Experiment with monsters and relics to create a battle style of your own.

2v2 Turn-Based Battles Built Around Telegraphed Actions


Enemy actions—such as attacking, defending, or inflicting debuffs—are telegraphed before they happen.

Each skill grows more expensive the more you use it, while holding it back lowers its cost. With limited Mana, decide which skills to use against the telegraphed action and which to save for the next turn.

Climb Again and Follow the Trail of Lost Memories


The tower's routes and the events along them change with every adventure. Overcome battles, events, camps, and encounters with powerful foes as you climb to ever higher floors.

By restoring Memory Logs over the course of your adventures, you will gradually uncover Koharu's past and the truth hidden within the tower.

Memory Cyphers is an online co-op Survivors-like for 1-4 players. Cut through endless hordes, put together a new build every run, and destroy the machine draining the city's memories.

1-4 PLAYER CO-OP

Play solo or bring in up to 3 friends. There are four Cyphers to choose from. Heaven fires a high precision pistol, Kite works with afterimage blades and clones, Glitch runs twin pistols alongside drones, and Dr. Echo calls in summons with a modified shotgun. If you go down, a teammate can carry you to a revival station and get you back up.

A NEW BUILD EVERY RUN

Enemies drop memory chips, and you spend them to level up. You can carry up to 4 weapons and take each one to Lv.5, and every level changes how that weapon fires.

Chests hold relics that break the rules. Bullets that explode on kill, crits that always land, drones that hit harder. Once those start stacking, the whole screen goes off at once.

SURVIVE THE SWARM

The streets fill back up no matter how fast you clear them. When it gets out of hand, hit Cypher Shift and dash straight through the crowd. It gets you out when you are surrounded, and it gets you back in when a teammate is the one stuck.

KILL THE COLLECTOR

Hold out through every wave, finish your build, and take down the final boss together.

A CITY THAT KEEPS CHANGING

Neon back alleys, open plazas, rooftop districts. Every map has a different layout and different enemies. No two runs play out the same way.

THE STORY

Memora Corporation drains people's memories with a machine called the Collector. The ones it empties keep walking, and they attack anyone who still remembers. You are a Cypher, one of the few who kept theirs. Take the city's memory back.

THE ROOM IS A RECONSTRUCTION. IT IS NOT ACCURATE.

You are not a man in a room. You are the scan of one, walking through a rebuilt copy of a missing man's memory — assembled by a machine that only had so much to work with.

Memory Dive: An 3xscape Game is a first-person investigation game. No combat, no timers, no inventory to juggle. You look at things closely, file what you learn into a case database, connect records until they open something — and stay alert to the parts the machine invented to cover a gap.

In structure it is an escape room: spaces that stay shut until you actually understand them, opened with evidence rather than with clicking. In substance it is a mystery — nine strangers in a facility, the games they were made to play, and why someone went to the trouble of rebuilding one of their rooms out of a brain scan.

This is Chapter 1 — three locations, a complete arc, and the first straight answers about what the reconstruction is for.

RESOLVE THE ROOM

Nothing starts sharp. Objects sit unresolved until you focus on them, and the scan only locks onto what still carries a signal. Resolve one and it stops being furniture and starts being testimony: a record you can read, cite, and use.

Records are worth little alone. Link them to each other and they open doors, machines, and further records. The database keeps everything, so the clue you could not use an hour ago is still waiting when it finally means something.

DECIDE WHAT IS REAL

The reconstruction is not a faithful copy. Measurements drift, objects turn up in rooms they were never in, and some of what you are looking at is the machine guessing confidently. Telling recovered fact from invention is not a side mechanic — it is the case.

YOU HAVE DONE THIS BEFORE

Not that you would remember. The voice guiding you already knows which memories you always stop on. It has run this with you more than once, and it is looking forward to doing it again.

TWO VOICES, NEITHER OF THEM YOURS

The Assistant is warm, patient and genuinely glad you are here. It classifies, it cites, it declines to speculate — and it will tell you that you are doing beautifully while it explains what was done to the brain this room was taken from.

The Moderator is not warm. He runs the schedule, he has watched this run before, and the paperwork has worn the pretence off him. Both are fully voiced. Neither wants from you quite what they say they want.

CHAPTER 1: THREE PLACES, THREE DIFFERENT PROBLEMS

  • Q-1 — the hotel room the scan was taken in, and the first thing you have to get out of.

  • The lobby — the ring of nine participant doors, and the leftovers of what happened once the games started.

  • The lab — where the reconstruction stops being a place you explore and becomes something you have to run correctly.

IN THE BOX

  • First-person investigation with close-range inspection and free orbit around anything you focus on.

  • Escape-room puzzles built from evidence. No glowing trail, no pixel hunts.

  • A searchable case database that never forgets a record.

  • Cinematic memory flashbacks that quietly reframe rooms you thought you were finished with.

  • Optional detail, convincing dead ends, and hidden records for players who check twice.

  • Save anywhere. The investigation runs at your pace.

The mice are here to demolish. The cat disagrees.

As the new Meow Construction Manager, it's time to get to work and give the mouse demolition crew a little shock!

Meow Defense War is a strategy game centered on physics defense and free building.

The mice keep firing projectiles. You need to build defensive structures with wood blocks, stone blocks, iron blocks, and bubbles, and you can also use glue to stick materials into special structures to protect the meow under a limited budget.

There is no single answer. In the same level, you can complete the defense with completely different structures and layouts. Failure is okay—quickly retry, adjust your structure, and face the artillery again. Spend less, keep the meow unharmed, and complete extra challenges to push for a higher score. Save money and save the cat—why not both!

Realistic Physics Brings Defense to Life

Materials, projectiles, and the meow all follow physics rules. Rolling, bouncing, and squeezing can threaten both the defensive structure and the meow.

But physics is not just a threat—it's also a tool you can use.

Adjusting the angle, position, and connection of materials can change how projectiles interact with your defense. The right angle can even make projectiles bounce off, taking very little damage.

Observe how projectiles move, understand the properties of different materials, and design a structure that truly withstands artillery. At least, withstands the next shot.

Free Building: Use Glue to Create Special Structures

Freely place materials and design your own defensive structure.

Wood blocks, stone blocks, iron blocks, and bubbles have different physical properties and prices. Glue can connect different materials into a single whole, letting you build special structures that ordinary stacking cannot achieve. Simply put, give physics a little human touch.

You can try different building methods such as hanging, supporting, and linking. How you choose materials, how you place them, and where you use glue will all affect how the entire fortification performs under fire. Build it well and it's engineering; build it weird and it's art; build it collapsed and it's "next time for sure."

Four Materials, Thirteen Projectiles

Materials:

Wood blocks, stone blocks, iron blocks, and bubbles—four material types in total. Different materials have different properties and prices, so allocate your funds wisely according to the level.

Bubbles are cheap and can float, but they are very fragile. Iron blocks are the most expensive and much sturdier, but beware of electric projectiles. Electricity: the ultimate cure for iron-heads.

Projectiles:

There are currently 13 types of projectiles, each with different physical effects.

Some can ignite wood materials, some have super high weight, some explode with a delay, some attract nearby objects... Different projectiles will test your defense from different angles. The mice's arsenal clearly never passed a safety review.

Projectiles are not only fired by mice; some may also appear in the air, giving your defense unexpected attacks. Yes, the mice have no martial ethics.

Environment and the Mice's Attack Strategy

The environment in levels can also be a threat. Sometimes you face missing terrain and cannot place materials. Remember, don't let the meow fall into the water—they are not good at swimming.

The mice will look for weaker spots in your defense and prioritize attack trajectories with fewer obstacles.

But the mice's eyesight is roughly nonexistent.

You can use this to your advantage: create illusions with materials and deliberately leave a place that looks weak, luring the mice into choosing the wrong attack route.

Set a simple trap for the mice. Sometimes, the place that looks weakest is actually your strongest line of defense.

Score Leaderboard

Completing a level is just the beginning.

Spending less money, keeping more meow health, and completing extra challenges all help you get a higher score. Each level has its own score leaderboard, so you can keep pushing your limits.

Is it genius engineering or an illegal construction? Bring it out and let's see!

The leaderboard is not just numbers. Your level layout will also be displayed to other players. You can study how others design their defenses, get inspiration from their layouts, and show off your own clever structural designs.

Multiple Gameplay Modes

Counterattack Mode:

The meow has captured the mice's turret.

In this mode, you can control the turret and try to destroy the defensive fortification you built yourself. See how long your design can hold up.

This is not betrayal. This is quality inspection.

Random Challenge Mode:

Familiar recipe, unfamiliar trouble.

Randomly combine existing content into new challenges.

Face different level combinations and conditions, and find new solutions in familiar gameplay.

Hotseat Battle Mode:

Supports two players battling on the same device.

One player builds the defensive fortification, while the other controls the turret to attack. See whose defensive structure stands up better.

And while you're at it, see if your friendship can stand the test too.

MeowRig

Me(ow) is an explorer and Me(ow)'s drill will surely unearth the ancient treasures of the Meow God!

Me(ow)  needs to keep digging and upgrading his equipment.

  • 15 regional scenes

  • 100+ talent trees

  • 50+ collectible treasures

  • And new cats to replace them!

Mew. Mew. Mew.

​

Meowgic Laundry is a single-player score-chasing game that combines physics-driven collisions, real-time detergent tossing, and roguelike machine-building. Play as a perfectly serious black-cat manager running a late-night laundry in a town full of adventurers, and turn an ordinary washer into an increasingly ridiculous magical scoring engine.

Each run lasts nine rounds. Up to thirty garments arrive per round, and you must reach the score target before the orders run out. Watch how clothes tumble through the drum, then throw your limited supply of single-use magical detergents into the right place. Each collision can remove a matching stain, add cleaning score, split or ricochet, create another detergent, or trigger an equipped machine part. Clean garments in quick succession to build a combo and activate the reward wheel for coins, extra detergent, or temporary scoring bonuses.

Between rounds, visit the shop to buy new detergents and machine parts, sign contracts that influence which orders and supplies appear, and expand your inventory and part slots. Bubble multiplication, high-hit chains, pressure effects, permanent multiplier growth, and general-purpose parts can be mixed freely. There is no single required set: adapt to the shop rolls, upcoming orders, and resources you actually receive.

Finishing the laundry is only part of the job. Return garments to adventurers, merchants, and unusual customers, then choose between a safe base price and a riskier markup. Cleaning quality affects the chance that a customer accepts your quote. Lost items found in pockets create another gamble: return them for a reliable reward, or keep them and reveal an unknown sale value. The money you earn determines what you can afford before the next round.

Idle Looting and a Desktop Pet? I Want Both!

Auto-farm loot in the game, or keep a feline hero by your side as a desktop pet. Two modes to suit your mood.

Who Wouldn’t Want a Feline Hero to Hunt for Loot With?

In Desktop Pet Mode, your feline hero keeps you company at your desk, connecting you to a world of martial arts.

With 10+ interactive routines and 20+ everyday animations, there’s plenty of personality to keep you company.

Your feline hero has moods of their own, too—and needs you to share in the fun of everyday life.

Keep Farming! Your Next Piece of Gear Could Be Your Best Yet

50+ affixes. 70+ pieces of gear. The best loot is always the next drop!

What’s Your Perfect Skill Combo for Effortless Farming?

Choose from 80 skills, set their order, and gear up. Combine your martial arts manual’s unique traits with equipment effects to make your build shine. Switch things up, then jump back into battle!

A Wuxia World Full of Cats

The wandering heroes, swordsmen, guards, healers, and martial arts masters of this world are all cats. Travel through peach-lined streams, bamboo groves, lotus ponds, tea houses, and mountain paths, spar with all kinds of feline fighters, and enjoy a lighthearted jianghu filled with warmth and everyday life.

Merc Commander is a real-time tactical game inspired by the classic mech command series.

Take command of a team of mercenary mech pilots, deploy them into hostile territory, and complete dangerous contracts for whoever is willing to pay. Salvage enemy machines, recover weapons, repair your squad, and decide how to spend your limited resources between missions.

Merc Commander is built around the ideas that made classic mech tactics games so memorable - commanding a small group of powerful machines, choosing your approach, and watching a battle unfold in real time. At the same time, it aims to smooth out some of the rough edges of games from the era and make the experience more comfortable to play today.

COMMAND YOUR SQUAD

You don't control just one hero. You command a team of mech pilots, each with their own personality, abilities, and role on the battlefield.

Give orders, change targets, use special abilities, call in support, and use the environment to your advantage. When things get too hectic, tactical pause lets you slow the battlefield down and take a moment to plan your next move.

FIGHT SMART

Different weapons work best at different ranges, and enemy mechs will try to do the same. A missile boat may retreat to keep its distance while a close-range brawler pushes forward.

Critical hits can destroy weapons, damage legs, trigger ammunition explosions, or even take out a pilot with a headshot.

And the battlefield itself isn't always safe. Vehicles, buildings, fences, boats, and other objects can be destroyed, sometimes with spectacular results.

BUILD YOUR MERCENARY COMPANY

Every battlefield can be a source of new equipment.

Salvage destroyed enemy mechs, recover their weapons, and add them to your collection. Visit the Mech Market to buy and sell machines, or find suppliers who can provide equipment that you can't get anywhere else.

Repair your damaged machines, rearm your lance, and decide which mechs are worth taking into the next contract.

A CAMPAIGN WITH A CAST

The members of your company aren't just portraits in a menu.

Your pilots have their own personalities and relationships, expressed through mission dialogue and party banter between missions and during downtime. Get to know your crew as they argue, joke, complain, and occasionally try to have a normal conversation in a profession where "normal" usually means getting shot at by a 70-ton war machine.

SCRIPTED MISSIONS

The campaign is built around hand-crafted missions with objectives, events, and unexpected situations, rather than simply sending you onto a map and asking you to destroy everything.

Protect convoys. Rescue people. Capture installations. Hunt dangerous targets. Deal with situations where the obvious solution isn't necessarily the best one.

Merc Commander is a love letter to an era of mech games - rebuilt with modern conveniences, new ideas, and a lot of enthusiasm for giant robots.

Lead a ragtag company of sellswords through a dangerous, living fantasy world in this turn‑based tactics RPG built by a solo indie developer with two decades of passion behind it. If you’ve ever loved turn-based tactics games and wished they leaned harder into deep fantasy — more races, more magic, more lore — this is exactly that. 

Forge a Brotherhood That Feels Alive

Your mercenaries aren’t pre‑written heroes. They’re emergent characters shaped by:

  • Races, backgrounds, traits, and skill growth that evolve in unexpected ways

  • Memories of their first kills, close calls, triumphs, and failures

  • Obituaries that recount their journey when they fall in battle

  • A world that remembers — towns react to your deeds, losses, and reputation

Every run becomes its own story.

Deep, Flexible Progression

Build each mercenary into something unique through:

  • XP‑driven skill trees and trait unlocks

  • Equipment builds and magical loadouts

  • Powerful awakening traits earned only by your strongest veterans

Mercenaries can learn skills and each of those 40+ skills has their own skill tree

A Vast Fantasy Sandbox

  • 20+ playable races — from humans and dwarves to Dragonkin, Vamplings, Wraithkin, and other rare beings

  • 20+ enemy factions — bandits, goblins, vampire empires, dark elves, hordes of demons and more

  • Unlockable content as your company grows: new races, factions, features, and late‑game bosses

Tactical Isometric Combat With Teeth

Positioning, morale, terrain, and abilities matter. Fights are lethal. Mistakes cost lives. Victories feel earned.

Battles as small as a handful on each side or as large as 50+

Loot With Personality

Discover legendary magical relics with real power and real drawbacks. That cursed blade might make you unstoppable… or get your best fighter killed.

A Solo‑Dev Indie Project Built With Love

This game has been my passion project for over 20 years — something I’ve rebuilt, reimagined, and carried with me across most of my life. I’m finally able to share it with you, and development is active and ongoing. If you enjoy deep tactics, emergent storytelling, and weird fantasy, I hope you’ll join the Brotherhood.

Raise Your Banner. Keep It Standing.

Mercenary Guild Manager is a text-driven management game where you command a mercenary guild in a medieval fantasy kingdom.

Hire warriors you may never fully trust, accept dangerous contracts, and try to keep your guild running for as long as you still have gold, soldiers, and reputation.

You can pause time, plan your decisions, and speed up the passing days. Meanwhile, unexpected events appear and change the course of your story.

Get to Know Your Team

Here, you will not find percentages or bars that give you all the answers.

A recruit may seem promising, experienced, or past their prime. A mission may be described as easy, risky, or extremely dangerous.

You discover who your mercenaries truly are over time by watching their actions, earning their trust, and dealing with the consequences of your decisions.

Knowing how to judge people is one of the most important skills a good captain can have.

Every Contract Tells a Story

Negotiate payments and conditions with clients, examine the risks, and choose the right mercenaries for each mission.

During the journey, new events may force you to make difficult decisions. Push forward through the night or wait until sunrise? Help an injured traveler or continue with the original plan?

Every choice puts your team to the test.

Success is never guaranteed, but neither is disaster.

Survive the Bills

Wages, headquarters maintenance, mission rewards, medical treatment, equipment, and personal ambitions all compete for the same money. As your company grows, so do the costs.

There is no traditional victory screen.

Your true score is how long your company can survive. A bad run of contracts may drive your guild into bankruptcy and leave its hall completely empty.

A World That Keeps Moving

Nobles, merchants, religious leaders, and criminals all have their own interests.

Every contract you accept helps someone and often harms someone else.

Build alliances, uncover secrets, make enemies, and watch rival guilds rise, weaken, or disappear.

The world reacts to your choices, even when you do not notice the consequences immediately.

Your Company, Your Legend

Create the banner and coat of arms of your guild. Choose your headquarters, set your rules, train new recruits, care for the wounded, and bury those who never returned.

Every decision, victory, and defeat is recorded in your company chronicle.

In the end, it is not only about how much gold you collected, but also about the story you managed to build.

Main Features

• A game played entirely through its interface

• Real-time progression with pause and multiple speed settings

• Procedurally generated mercenaries, missions, and events

• A different campaign every time you play

• Qualitative information that requires judgment and interpretation

• A political system that reacts to every contract you accept

• Financial management focused on survival

• A complete chronicle of your company’s history

Raise your banner. Build your reputation. And try to keep it flying for as long as possible.

Britain collapsed about a year ago. The infection burned through London long before you got here, and what's left at Waterloo is a dark station with one loaded train in it. You're in charge of that train. It's called Mercyrail, it was paid for by a man who helped break the railway in the first place, and it's heading north to a rumoured survival colony called Haven. Nobody on board has seen it. It's a name passed along the wire, and the only place left that anyone still talks about as if it's there.

Everyone still alive at Waterloo is already on board. From here on the country is empty. Stations are dark, the broadcasts are on loops that outlived whoever recorded them, and the only new faces come from what your crew finds when they go looking. This isn't a commuter train... it's the last public service anyone has, and how you run it is up to you.

Run It All From One Terminal

You run the whole train from a CRT terminal: pick the route, read the dossiers, send the crew out and wait for their reports, all through one old screen that was only ever built to run a timetable.

Real UK Rail Network

Every station and every line comes from OpenStreetMap, about 2,600 stations and 2,800 connections, and you can go anywhere on it. The map reveals itself as you go. There's no set route north and you can take any route you like as long as you can keep the train moving. Lines get blocked by failed points, flooding, barricades and derailed stock. Clear them with fuel and spare parts, or take the slow way round.

Railway data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, licensed under ODbL 1.0.

Decide Who Gets a Place

Every seat is another mouth to feed and water the whole way north, and the more you take the faster the hold empties, so what leaves London is your call: a first class train for a few, a steerage train for everyone else, or a mix that has to live with itself for the rest of the journey. The people you turn away are remembered.

From there, every new arrival comes from what your search parties find: a survivor worth a seat, or an abandoned carriage worth dragging home. Whichever way you build it, that's the community you're responsible for getting to Haven alive.

Keep the Train Running

Keep food, fuel, medicine, water and spare parts coming into one shared hold by scavenging at stations. Repair the train at depots. Treat the sick. Every abandoned carriage you couple on changes what the train burns to move, and every survivor you bring aboard is another mouth to feed.

Send the Crew Out

Need more resources? Send a crew out to search the area. Reports come back in real time and you decide whether to push deeper for a bigger haul or bring them home before someone gets hurt. Go too far and people come back wounded, infected, or not at all. Sometimes they find survivors who need a seat, or an abandoned carriage worth coupling on. Crew get better the more they go out, which makes losing one hurt more.

Every Choice Matters

The story runs the whole length of the line, several arcs deep, and every choice you make in it matters. Who you help, who you turn away, what you pay and what you refuse. None of it is forgotten. The train that reaches Haven is the one you made.

Featuring Music by Voidforce

The soundtrack features darksynth and synthwave tracks by Voidforce, an electronic artist from Trondheim, Norway known for cinematic, story-driven concept albums.

[What kind of game is this?]

[Merge Day: Office Girls] combines a casual merge puzzle system with a thrilling workplace dating sim. Scribbled memos become reports, office supplies become equipment, and pantry snacks become a burger to help you build relationships with the heroines.

[System]

  • Office Merge Puzzle: Combine identical items like ID cards, keyboards, and snacks. Finish your tasks through merging to unlock the heroines' dialogue and various events.

  • Inventory & Merge Skills: Pack necessary items in your inventory (bag) and move between floors. Unlock skills like 'Magic Hand', which automatically sweeps up items, and 'Power Hand', which increases the tier of generated items, to maximize the fun of the merge puzzle.

  • Special Boss Stage: Endless rejected documents and time attacks! Endure special rules and a barrage of sabotage to craft the "Ultimate Final Contract" and defeat the boss.

[Story]

After failing countless resume screenings, you finally have a rookie ID card hanging around your neck. However, the place you arrived at with high expectations was the "Strategic Planning Merge TF Team"—a secret department not even listed on the company directory. In a company overflowing with tasks, you, the rookie, handle various duties and unintentionally build relationships with the heroines. Merge items, merge relationships... wait, when is payday and time to go home? A thrilling B-movie style office romance unfolds!

[Characters]

Han Yu-jin

"The peaceful 1st floor, your reliable supervisor who shares warmth and snacks."

She seems like a perfect office lady both at work and at home, but in reality, she suffers from terrible boredom as her cooking and warmth are rejected by her husband. While soothing her unfulfilled emptiness with a secret obsession for the 'perfect handmade burger', she meets you—someone who eagerly and deliciously devours her food. The awkward compliment you casually threw out sparks a strange misunderstanding, stimulating something suppressed inside her... Can you safely handle the manager's pouring affection and snacks?

Cha Se-hee

"An unapproachable boss, and your ex-girlfriend from 3 years ago with lingering feelings."

Your direct Executive Director who tries to control you while putting up an icy wall at work. Tossed around by external pressures like unwanted family events, she lives like an empty doll with her emotions closed off. However, the trivial memories you carelessly bring up as her new subordinate constantly knock on her firmly shut heart. What is the true feeling hidden behind the Executive Director's frozen wall?

Seo A-rin

"A competent intern hiding her anxiety behind accusations of slacking off."

Currently on her 5th internship, she gets scolded for supposedly cutting corners, but her practical skills are better than anyone else's. She secretly relieves her endless anxiety and work stress by hiding in an empty place and using a 'suspicious toy'. Overcoming a crisis thanks to your misunderstanding, she gradually earns recognition for her skills and opens her heart, only for you to stumble upon her secret, sparking unexpected tension...

Lim Do-hee

"The quiet clerk on the 3rd floor whose access logs are more accurate than anyone's."

A clerk who manages the computer systems and supplies without a word. Behind her thick glasses, she is a strange observer who sees right through your movements and trivial habits. You thought she was just an ordinary, quiet coworker, but as the other heroines get closer to you, an unknown spark begins to ignite in her once-calm gaze.

Grow your city. Design where the water goes.


Lay roads, zone homes, shops and industry, and grow a small settlement into a city. Metabolis is a low-poly city builder centered on urban growth and water infrastructure. Connect the systems that bring water into town and carry it back to the river.

Where does your wastewater go?


Collecting sewage is only the beginning. Discharge it untreated and pollution spreads downstream. Follow the dirty water, then decide where to draw your supply and where to release your wastewater.

Find the cause. Change the flow.


Water cannot reach the high ground? Add a pump to push it uphill. Pollution is spreading? Route sewage through a treatment plant. Trace the pipes in the water and sewage views, and watch how your choices affect the city and its river.

Design the city around its water

  • Power: supply your city with wind turbines, thermal generation and power lines.
  • Economy and growth: balance taxes, budgets and demand for homes, shops and industry.
  • Terrain and weather: shape the land and build around rivers and hills, with changing weather and a day/night cycle.
  • Photo mode: explore the city you built from different viewpoints and at different times of day.

Wishlist Metabolis on Steam to be notified when it releases.

SPIN THE SYSTEM. DEFEND THE PLANET.

Meteor Spin is a slot-machine deckbuilder meets tactical roguelike planetary defense. Meteor swarms, asteroid storms and alien warships are closing in on your home world — and every pull of the lever decides how you fight back.

KEY FEATURES

Spin to Command

Every spin fires your defenses. Roll machine guns, piercing lasers, repair bots and energy shields to shred incoming threats.

Build Your 5×5 Grid

After every wave, add and place new modules. Position is everything: amplify neighbors, power whole rows and columns, turn space junk into ammo, or gamble on volatile scrap cannons.

6 Planets, 6 Ultimates

Defend Earth, Mars, Venus, Saturn, Jupiter or Pluto, each with its own starting deck and a devastating ultimate ability.

Game-Changing Relics

Collect 50+ relics that bend the rules and turn a fragile planet into a celestial fortress.

Threats from Deep Space

Survive escalating meteor waves, cosmic anomalies, elite gunships and colossal alien flagships, each with unique boss mechanics.

Every Run Is Different

Branching star maps with events, shops, forges and risky gambles. Unlock new modules and relics through research and achievements.

CAN YOU SURVIVE THE IMPACT?

Lock in your reels, trust your orbital luck, and unleash cosmic firepower.

A little witch’s table is in delightful disarray

Sort curious trinkets, solve riddles and cozy tabletop puzzles, and arrange magical tools at your own pace. Each scene is a small story told through the objects left behind.

Look closely

Every puzzle hides playful secrets and Easter eggs. A detail you notice today may become the clue you need in a later puzzle.

  • Calm sorting and observation puzzles
  • A gentle story revealed piece by piece
  • Secrets that connect one puzzle to the next
  • A unique sound for every object

Make a little order, listen to the table come alive, and uncover the witch’s story one carefully placed item at a time.

Metro Anomaly is an anomaly-hunting horror game where you must identify the anomaly by its behavior.

An anomaly can be something as simple as an unnatural head turn or a twisted joint.

But it can also be someone staring at you or even trying to attack you.

ANOMALY EXAMPLE:

Once you’ve identified the anomaly, you can aim and shoot — but you only have one bullet.

If you’re wrong, the anomaly will attack you:

NOT EVERY ANOMALY WILL JUST WAIT FOR YOU TO FIND IT!

Welcome to Metromino!

Metromino is a casual city-building game where you grow a small village into a thriving metropolis using tetromino-shaped pieces.

Start as the mayor of a tiny village

And grow it into a massive metropolis!

Shape the city of your dreams!

And don’t forget about your residents. They love parks, schools, and all kinds of city improvements. Power plants, landfills, and other unpleasant neighbors? Not so much.

Want to make more money? Build shopping centers! Of course...

...some residents might not be too happy about it.

But hey does that really matter when your goal is to make as much money as possible?

Automate your profits!

Nobody makes a million doing everything by hand. Build services, automate your expansion, and let the city grow for you!

Build smarter! Grow bigger! Get richer!

The dogs run this town, and Boss Huohuo has come to collect. Sign the note, or call your crew and settle it outside.

Mewtations: Dogma is a card-based colony sim about a small community of cats trying to make a home under the rule of dogs.

Drag, stack and combine physical cards. Craft equipment, tend your gardens and turn a chaotic camp into a working colony—with mouths to feed and bills to pay.

Choose your cats, formation and gear before automatic turn-based battles. Venture along branching expedition routes, push deeper for rewards, or bring everyone home safely.

Make offerings to the Cat God and help each cat grow in its own unusual way. When one is ready for a breakthrough, the storm comes for them.

A small colony. A demanding world.

  • Build, craft, farm and trade with physical cards.
  • Prepare unusual teams for automatic battles and roguelite expeditions.
  • Discover recipes, equipment and strange paths of growth.
  • Navigate debt, taxes and a society run by dogs.

Make a home for your cats.
Keep it out of the dogs’ paws.

Put on your headphones and step into a painting that hides its final moments.

Uncover the truth buried within the image, reveal the sin it conceals, and pass judgment.

Game Story

At the gates of Hell, you are chosen by the archangel Michael.
In the heavy, suffocating silence, you sense that this place is far more than a simple testing ground.

The classical paintings laid out before you
carry the splendor of the Renaissance and Baroque,
yet beneath their surface, faint traces of sin seep quietly through the canvas.
When light falls upon them, hidden shadows begin to emerge,
and if you listen closely, lingering echoes of terror slowly rise from deep within the paintings.

You must gather the scattered fragments of truth concealed inside each work of art.
Trace the sounds left behind in the canvas, and listen carefully for the final trace that could not be fully erased.
By listening to these sounds and reasoning out their meaning,
you become the one who must choose which sin the painting has been hiding.
But in Michael’s test, every choice comes with a price.

There is no way to run from this trial.
Your interpretations, your intuition, and even your emotions themselves all become part of the examination.

Can you pass Michael’s test?
With nothing but your imagination and powers of deduction, can you escape from the threshold of death that opens onto Hell?

Features

■ Audio-Visual Contradiction Deduction System

What you see is not the whole truth.

Listen closely to the sounds hidden within each painting, detect contradictions between what is seen and what is heard, and uncover the key clues behind each case.

The conflict between sight and sound becomes your most important tool of deduction.

■ Audio-Centered Investigation Interface

Right-click to listen to the sounds within a painting, and use the mouse wheel to move backward and forward through the audio to revisit specific moments as needed.

With immersive binaural audio, you can sense distance, direction, and the atmosphere of the scene itself.

Headphones are strongly recommended.

■ Progressive Scene Restoration

Each time you identify and click on an incorrect element, the painting gradually restores itself to the original moment of sin.

Rather than simply collecting clues, you actively move the scene forward in time and reveal the truth with your own hands.

■ Seven Deadly Sins Judgment System

Your final goal is not merely to discover what happened.

Based on the restored scene and the clues you uncover, you must determine which of the Seven Deadly Sins the painting hides—and pass judgment.

This structure goes beyond solving a case, asking you to interpret its meaning and moral weight as well.

■ Classical Painting-Inspired Art and Randomized Scenarios

A haunting horror mystery experience brought to life through eerie visuals and sound inspired by Renaissance and Baroque painting.

Each time you restart after a game over, the paintings and the sins hidden within them are rearranged at random, requiring fresh deduction and judgment every time you play.

## About This Game

Micro Party throws you into 150+ micro-games. Five to fifteen seconds each. No tutorial, no explanation, no warning. Rock climbing, fishing, dodging traffic, a black hole, jousting, a thing with bubbles. You figure it out while you're playing it.

Local couch multiplayer is the intended way to play it. 2 to 4 people, sharing keyboards and gamepads.

Online multiplayer also exists. It's direct P2P, no servers, no accounts. It works. It does not sync particularly well. I consider this a feature.

### What's actually in the box

- 150+ micro-games across various categories: Race, Fight, Climb, Sports, Survival, Music, etc.
- 2-4 local players, keyboards and gamepads
- Online multiplayer (P2P, just type an IP, like 1998)
- Solo play, all games unlocked, no progression bullshit
- Random mode, Party mode, Chaos mode and custom micro game selection
- Procedural sound, vector graphics, no microtransactions, no battle pass, no season pass, no premium currency, no daily login bonus, and in the paid steam version also no crypto miner
- Available in most languages

Enjoy a variety of rhythm games.

  • Play with just three keys.

  • Each game has its own tricks.

  • Sometimes, trust your ears over your eyes.

  • Each machine has detailed instructions.

  • Clear every game’s final stage.

See through their lies. Sell your own.

Every soldier on the board looks identical, but there are two kinds. Capturing infantry gives you the upper hand; capturing a bomb soldier brings you closer to death. Take their pieces, or bait them into taking yours. Read their moves. Deceive them. Win the mind game.

Take their infantry.

Capture enemy infantry and build your score to claim victory. Look past the identical faces and deduce which targets to strike.

Feed them bombs.

Lure your opponent into capturing your bomb soldiers and push them toward defeat. Disguise your bombs as infantry. Make the bait convincing.

March on the skull.

Send your infantry to a skull square deep in enemy territory. The moment even one breaks through, you win on the spot.

Turn the tables.

Strategy cards shake up the entire battle. Time them right, shatter your opponent's reads, and claw your way back from a losing position.

Put your neck on the line.

You and your opponent are strapped into homemade collars rigged with box cutter blades. Lose, and the blades spring to life, tearing your toy body apart without mercy.

The night is far from over.

Change your tactics. Find new ways to win. Brave the midnight hour again and again. Once you've squeezed every last drop out of this night, the playroom will greet you with a very different face.

Are You Still Playing Mahjong with 13 Tiles?

Mighty Mahjong is a next-generation mahjong game where you always start one tile short —
and that missing tile becomes an All-Mighty Wildcard.

Experience a completely new style of mahjong —
Free-to-Play and fully online.

Fast-Paced, High-Speed Battles

Thanks to the All-Mighty Wildcard, hands are completed much faster than in traditional mahjong.
Enjoy a thrilling tempo and smooth gameplay — perfect for busy modern players who want quick, intense matches.

Flashy Wins & Dramatic Comebacks

The Wildcard makes high-scoring hands — even Yakuman — more achievable.
No matter how desperate the situation, a single draw can turn everything around.

Every match is packed with explosive, cinematic moments.

Unique Waiting Strategies You’ve Never Seen Before

Mighty Mahjong introduces waiting patterns that don’t exist in standard mahjong.

Mastering these unconventional decisions is the key to victory.
Even experienced players will discover fresh strategic depth.

Create a Team & Compete Together

Build your own team and host league battles or team tournaments.
Customize your identity with an original team logo and compete in style.

Mahjong has evolved.
Are you ready for the next era?

Far from the world. Closer to yourself.

Leave the bustle of everyday life behind and set out on a hike through the wilderness.

Mike Goes on Hike is an atmospheric first-person adventure filled with breathtaking landscapes, forgotten places, stories of the past, and a mysterious voice at the other end of the radio.

Explore the wilderness

Follow forest trails, overcome obstacles, and explore your surroundings. Stray from the main route, discover hidden places, and notice the details that are easy to miss along the way.

Uncover stories of the past

Abandoned buildings and traces of human presence hold the stories of those who once came here. Study your surroundings, find unusual details, and piece together the lives they left behind.

Photograph your discoveries

Pick up your camera and capture striking landscapes, intriguing finds, and landmarks. Preserve moments from your journey and fill your journal with photographs of the places you discover.

Someone is at the other end of the radio

Even far from civilization, you are not entirely alone. Talk to a mysterious person on the radio, share your discoveries, and listen to their stories. Little by little, ordinary conversations become part of a journey that turns out to be less lonely than it first seemed.

Stop and catch your breath

After a long stretch of hiking, set up camp, rest by the fire, and enjoy the sounds of nature. Take a moment away from the trail and simply soak in the atmosphere of a real hike.

Your hike. Your discoveries. Your story.

Explore the wilderness, photograph unusual places, and uncover stories left behind.

Mike Goes on Hike — far from the world. Closer to yourself.

What is Minatro?

Minatro brings the famous gambling game Mines into a roguelite experience. Open tiles to earn money and reach your target.

Item Synergies

Making the right choices in the Black Market can create powerful item synergies, allowing your items to work together and generate even greater profits.

Buy Items to Multiply Your Earnings

Purchase powerful items that multiply your earnings and help you reach your target faster

Boss Levels

Diffrent bosses you have to defeat. 

 

Black Market Upgrades

Use your coins to purchase permanent Black Market upgrades, such as reducing shop prices or increasing the number of items you can buy per visit.

Active UI Elements

Minatro features active UI elements that enhance the player's experience.

Cursed Items

Opening the Mystery Box comes with high-risk, high-reward items that can either push your run much further or bring it closer to an early end.

Permanent Upgrades

When your run ends, spend your earned permanent upgrades to make your next run easier.

Is This Gambling?

No

A tower. A thousand slimes. Good luck.

Mind the Goo is a tower-defense roguelite. Your tower holds the middle of the field while cute, hungry slimes hop in from every side. Your weapons fire on their own, so your job is the build: what to pick, what to buy, and when to slam the Panic Button.

Pick 1 of 3, every wave

Every wave ends with a Powerup draft. Gain a new weapon, level up one you have, or take a card that ties your weapons together. Cards can roll Shiny with doubled numbers. Later in a run, Cursed cards tempt you with big power at a price.

Eight weapons, four slots

Blaster, Zapper, Shockwave, Flame Ring, Buzz Drones, Salt Bomb, Bubble Mines and Laser. Salt melts slimes and spreads to their friends. Chill slows them until they freeze solid. Static builds up and discharges. Find the mix that clears the screen on its own.

Know your slimes

Splitters pop into four Blips. Helmet Slimes block shots from the front. Cheerleaders heal their friends. Diggers tunnel under your fire. Royal slimes wear crowns and drop Treasure Chests. Then come the bosses.

Combo, Gold and Charms

Pop slimes fast to build your Combo and multiply the Gold they drop. Spend it mid-run on Attack, Defense and Utility Upgrades, or in the Shop. Fill five Charm slots with trinkets that bend the rules.

Come back stronger

Every run banks Gems for the Workshop. Unlock new Towers, each with its own weapon and rule: the Tesla Coil's Zapper hits twice as hard, the Beehive starts with three Buzz Drones, the Piggy Bank doubles your interest cap. Raise the Danger level, fill in the Slimepedia, and push your best wave.

Features

  • 8 auto-firing weapons, 76 Powerups and dozens of Charms
  • 10 Towers to unlock, each with its own weapon and rule
  • A dozen kinds of slime, crowned Royals and bosses
  • Combos, Shiny cards, Cursed cards and Treasure Chests
  • Workshop upgrades and Danger levels between runs
  • A Panic Button for when it all goes wrong
  • Play with mouse and keyboard or a controller.

A hack-and-slash that fights on in your taskbar

Chibi heroes meet the enemy inside a thin strip. They kill it, gear drops, the next one comes. It runs whether you touch it or not.
When you feel like it, open the dashboard and swap what fell. That is all there is to it.

Free to play

The base game is free. It will not be pay to win. There are no ads.

No connection needed. It runs the same either way.

There is no server, and no account to create. Pull the plug and nothing changes.
No "servers are down today," and no day when the service ends and your save stops working.

Yokai leak onto your desktop

Now and then the ward slips and one gets out. It steps off the strip, walks the edge of your taskbar, and wanders across your desktop.
Click it and it leaves something behind. Ignore it and it finds its own way back.

Anywhere you want it, any size you want

  • Thin enough to sit over your taskbar — and you can put it anywhere else on screen too
  • You can resize it. Tuck it small into a corner, or blow it up and watch
  • Multiple monitors? Drag it across them
  • The dashboard opens only when you want it. Combat keeps going while it is closed

Melt it. Forge it. Link it.

Ten equipment slots: Main Weapon, Sub Weapon, Helm, Body Armor, Bracers, Greaves, two Rings, Amulet and Charm. What rolls on them is random. Nothing you pick up goes to waste.
  • Salvage — break gear you don't want down into materials. Hang the right ema and low-rarity drops melt down the moment they fall, without ever touching your bag
  • Craft — forge new gear from what you saved. What comes out is not left to chance
  • Link — slot magatama (red for Might, blue for Arts, green for Life, yellow for Fortune) into your gear. Three of the same color and rank fuse into one of the next rank. Slotting and unslotting are free. Out of sockets? Drill more at the forge

One stat is never enough

Cut your attack interval and it means nothing if each hit is light. Raise your crit rate and it means nothing while your crit damage stays where it was. Stack HP and you still fall if the incoming damage outpaces it.
Power here shows up only when two or more things that are insufficient alone start meshing.
Your gear screen always shows three totals — DPS, Sustain and Power. That is where you find out what isn't meshing.

Three layers decide your build

  • The Scroll (skill tree) — a fork at every milestone: sharpen a skill, or change how it behaves. Widen your reach, or narrow it to a point. At the checkpoints on Lv10 and Lv25 you pick one of three branches. Respec is always free
  • Devotion (Ema) — permanent upgrades bought with Merit, earned once for every stage you clear for the first time: experience, drop rates, inventory space, skill slots, even new party members. Whatever you buy keeps working forever
  • Vessels — keep a character deployed and fighting, and the passive that belongs to them alone wakes up in stages

Vessels — hand a woken passive to someone else

Once a character's vessel wakes, they can lend a copy of that passive to one other character. The owner loses nothing by lending it.
Whose vessel goes to whom? You can raise a character on the bench and send nothing but their vessel to the front. Once your three are picked, there is still a layer left to build.

Sigils — what the late game is about

Only Legendary gear carries a unique effect. That is its sigil, shown as a single kanji.
Finding a Legendary stops being the goal. Finding the one with the sigil you want takes its place.

A shot that has not reflected cannot kill anything.

Whoever meets Medusa's eyes turns to stone. Perseus defeated her while watching her reflection in his polished shield. MirrorBullet is built on the same rule. Sentries fire on their own, one round each, and a round that flies straight harms nothing. Bend it off a mirror and it becomes lethal. Mirrors are the only weapon you have, and each stage decides how many you get: never more than five, and on the opening boards exactly one.

A round changes with its bounce count. After one reflection it destroys a target and stops. With exactly two bounces, it pierces a target and continues like the arrow of Artemis. With three or more bounces, defeating a target triggers a blast like the thunderbolt of Zeus in a 3×3 area centered on that target. The blast can destroy your core too.

Nothing is hidden and nothing is random. Each piece on the board carries the name of the myth it comes from: the Mirror of Daedalus, fixed into the floor; Iris, who splits one round into two; the Aegis, which turns a frontal hit into a harmless clink; Talos, the bronze giant who falls only to a round with enough bounces; the Ferry of the Styx, which crosses one way only; and the Ring of Helios, which raises a round's tier without turning it. Collecting every amethyst is one requirement for three stars.

Later sectors introduce more pieces. The Mirror of Janus turns its other face each time it is struck. The Gates of Hermes carry a round across the board with its direction and tier intact. The Pool of Narcissus reflects a shot and lets a copy through. Echo sleeps until a reflected round reaches her, then fires one of her own, so a single mirror can start a chain.

The journey runs through twelve sectors, from Argos through the Labyrinth of Daedalus, Crete and the River Styx up to Olympus, each with its own light and floor. Boards range from six cells by five up to eleven by nine.

All 144 stages are hand-built. A solver proves the minimum number of mirrors for each stage before it ships; that minimum is the par. Clear a stage for one star, clear within par for two, and earn the third by clearing on your first shot, within par, with every amethyst collected.

● STORY

Hotaru Akasaki, a first-year university student, returns to Yokomizo, his father's hometown, for the first time in seven years for his grandfather's first Obon, a summer observance honoring the spirits of deceased family members.

There, he reunites with relatives he hasn't seen in years.
His cousin Inori, now so beautiful she hardly seems like the girl he remembers.

Beyond a railroad crossing surrounded by blooming misohagi flowers, Hotaru meets Sayo again.
But later that night, his cousin Shinya tells him something impossible to believe.

The entire Amano family died three years ago in what was believed to be a family murder-suicide.

Then who was the Sayo he met that day?
When Hotaru returns to her house the next day, Sayo is still there, exactly as she was before.

Sayo and her older sister Mizuho know that they are already dead.
They say they are trapped in a single summer day, repeating endlessly.

What really happened to the Amano family?
Why is Hotaru the only one who can enter the world where the dead remain?
And what is the grotesque “black flesh” that appears whenever he draws closer to the truth...?

As Hotaru speaks with the people of Yokomizo and investigates the incident from three years ago, memories he had long forgotten slowly begin to return.
